output.title: Replace open-graph-scraper and cheerio with node-html-parser
output.body:
The scraper used two separate libraries — open-graph-scraper for OG metadata and cheerio for the Amazon image fallback — which meant two dependencies and two code paths for what is really one job. - `package.json` drops `cheerio` and `open-graph-scraper`, adds `node-html-parser ^8.0.4`; `jest.config.mjs` transformIgnorePatterns gains `node-html-parser` and `entities`.

Not tested: `scrape.test.ts` and `scrapeRoute.test.ts` were updated to mock `global.fetch` instead of `ogs`, but I didn't run `npm test` in this session — worth confirming the suite passes before merge.

original.title: Add GET /api/devices/{device_name}/arc-status endpoint for Azure Arc connection status

output.title: Add Azure Arc connection status to the device dashboard
output.body:
Devices are Arc-connected (host, VM, K8s cluster) but the dashboard had no way to show whether that connection was actually up. This adds an ARM-backed status endpoint and wires it into the frontend badge that used to show raw MQTT online/offline.

Backend:
- New `GET /api/devices/{device_name}/arc-status` in `devices.py`, auth via `ClaimsDep`, looks up hub/country from Eventhouse then calls `ArcStatusReader.get_arc_status()`
- `ArcStatusReader` (`app/services/arc_status_reader.py`) queries ARM with `DefaultAzureCredential`; `derive_resource_names()` turns `atl-azureiot-vm-k3s` into host=`azureiot`, vm=`azureiot-vm`, k8s=`atl-azureiot-vm-k3s`; `build_resource_group()` maps hub/country to `EXP-MFG-AIO-{HUB}-{COUNTRY}-RG`
- If hub is missing from the Eventhouse record (device not found or a Kusto error), the route falls back to deriving hub from the name prefix before the first `-`; country defaults to `US` when absent
- ARM 404 on either resource raises `LookupError` → HTTP 404; any other ARM failure → HTTP 502
- New `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` setting, added to `Settings`, `.env.example`, and `dependencies.get_arc_status_reader()` (lru_cache singleton)

Frontend:
- `App.jsx` fetches arc status per device once after the initial device list loads (`loadArcStatus`), separate from the 30s MQTT status poll, since ARM calls are slower and change less often
- `DeviceCard` and `DeviceDetailPage` replace the old online/partial/offline LED badge with an `azure-status-badge` showing connected/offline/partial/not-implemented, derived from host+vm+k8s status plus recent message counts (`deriveAzureStatus`)
- The "hide offline" filter (`isDeviceNotImplemented`) now hides devices with no usable arc status instead of MQTT-offline devices; button label changes to "Hidden" / "Hide not implemented devices"

`DeviceDetailPage` duplicates the connected/disconnected derivation logic inline instead of reusing `deriveAzureStatus` from `DeviceCard.jsx` — worth pulling into a shared helper in a follow-up.

Tested: none of the automated tests were run in this session; `tests/test_arc_status.py` covers the happy path, 404s, 502s, and hub/country fallback with `FakeArcStatusReader`/`FakeStatusReaderForArc` stubs and should be run with `pytest` before merge. Frontend changes have not been exercised in a browser.

original.title: Add durable provider-neutral Issue dispatch guard

output.title: Add durable provider-neutral Issue dispatch guard
output.body:
Closes #2077. Adds `IssueDispatchGuard`, a durable admission authority for one logical Issue implementation attempt, so a local run and a remote provider run for the same Issue can no longer both start or silently overwrite each other's ownership.

- `IssueDispatchGuard` (`src/auto_coder/issue_dispatch.py`) writes an incarnation-scoped claim to SQLite before any remote callback runs; only an adapter-classified `NOT_STARTED` observation durably releases it, and pending/accepted/indeterminate/failed/deferred claims all suppress every other candidate, including local ones and other providers.
- Consumers get a structured `DispatchResult` (identity, backend, provider, provider reference, diagnostic, `claim_incarnation`, `tracking_complete`) instead of parsed action strings; `LOCAL_COMPLETED` only means the synchronous call finished, not that anything merged.
- CloudRun and `cloud.csv` records migrate into the same table as suppressing evidence: contradictory run/binding references defer, and an attempt-unassociated `cloud.csv` binding blocks automatic dispatch unless the caller passes `authorize_new_attempt=True`, in which case the old binding stays inspectable in `legacy_issue_dispatch_ownership` rather than moving to the new attempt.
- Storage failures — SQLite unavailable before a claim, or an `OSError` mid-finalization — fail closed to `DEFERRED`/`INDETERMINATE` with a diagnostic, and never invoke the adapter callback twice (`test_storage_failures_fail_closed_before_submission_and_after_observation`).
- `docs/client-features/provider-neutral-issue-dispatch-handoffs.md` and `docs/dashboard-observability.md` record that this is an adapter-stage boundary only: it isn't wired into ordinary Issue dispatch yet and adds no new dashboard projection.

Follow-up: candidate selection and integration into ordinary Issue processing, plus the resulting dashboard trace, are left to the next adapter/integration stage.

Tested: `bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue_dispatch.py` and `bash scripts/test.sh -m "not browser and not opencode_live"`.

output.title: Add electrolysis controller I2C protocol and module scaffolding
output.body:
Adds the I2C command/status contract and polling module for a dedicated electrolysis ESP32 controller, wires it into `PoolLogicModule` and `IOModule`, documents the design, and adds `AGENTS.md` with Cursor Cloud build/test instructions for future agents.

- The I2C contract (`ElectrolysisProtocol.h`) defines a 19B `CommandFrame` and 23B `StatusFrame` with CRC8, preferred address `0x43` (alt `0x45`), and clamped production/deadtime/window/temp values.
- `ElectrolysisModule` polls the controller every 100–5000ms (default 500ms) and exposes `ElectrolysisService` under `ServiceId::Electrolysis`; config persists under new NVS keys `el_en`/`el_addr`/`el_poll`/`el_mcur`.
- `IOModule` gains a raw I2C write+read op, `ioI2cTransfer_`, guarded by the existing IO bus mutex and exposed via `IOServiceV2::i2cTransfer` for other modules to reuse.
- `PoolLogicControl.cpp` pushes SWG-driven production demand to the electrolysis service through `writeElectrolysisRequest_()`, and drops the heater auto-mode block (`heaterDesired`/`heaterFsm_`) from the control loop.
- `docs/core/electrolysis-controller.md` (287 lines) records the design status ("integration FlowIO démarrée, firmware du controleur reste a implementer"), I2C addressing guidance, and the state machine; `docs/README.md` and the `FlowIOBootstrap` module order now reference it.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the PlatformIO build/lint/test workflow for Cursor Cloud agents and flags a known build break: `ElectrolysisModule.cpp` references `LogModuleIdValue::ElectrolysisModule`, which isn't yet defined in `src/Core/LogModuleIds.h`.

Firmware won't build until that enum entry is added; `AGENTS.md` calls this out as the only blocker found so far.

Tested: PlatformIO Core 6.1.19 installed and the ESP32 toolchain compiles; the native unit test `test_poollogic_filtration_window` passed 5/5. Did not build any `FlowIO`/`Supervisor` environment, since it currently fails on the missing `LogModuleIds.h` enum entry.

original.title: bridge-site: serve guest HTTP through service workers

output.title: Add bridge-site: browser bridge for guest HTTP
output.body:
Adds the deployment-specific browser bridge on top of linux-guest's HTTP adapters (#121): a service worker per guest origin that serves guest HTTP responses into real browser navigations, with a rendezvous protocol so a guest origin can find and bind to an open VM tab. Wires the demo into the site hero and deploys the bridge from CI.

- Rendezvous: `serveGuest()` is the client package's only public entry point. One tab wins a Web Lock keyed to the hub origin and becomes the provider; other guest origins broadcast demands over `BroadcastChannel("linux-bridge-rendezvous-v1")` via provider/requester iframes until the provider binds them.
- Service worker: registers per-origin at `/_bridge_sw.js` (scope `/`) and pins the embedding VM origin from its first `postMessage`, refusing any other origin's port. It shares five status pages (`BRIDGE_BAD_PORT`, `BRIDGE_CONNECTING`, `BRIDGE_NO_VM`, `BRIDGE_RELAY_TIMEOUT`, `GUEST_ERROR`) with the static `index.html` fallback; the `frame-ancestors` CSP backstop is left as a TODO in `public/_headers`.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` adds a `deploy-bridge` job that publishes `packages/bridge-site/public` to Cloudflare Pages project `linux-bridge` via `wrangler`. The workflow still has `# TODO(tom): create this Pages project`, so the job won't succeed until that project exists.
- Test config: `playwright.config.js` runs chromium and firefox only, since WebKit can't resolve `*.localhost` subdomains, and forces `ThirdPartyStoragePartitioning` on in chromium to match real Chrome instead of Playwright's relaxed default.
- The site hero now embeds the guest demo through this client package (`packages/site`).

This branch also carries #121's commits (linux-guest HTTP adapters, the apk/apk-tools packaging rework, and the package.nix/vm-test churn across the tree) until it merges; review here is scoped to bridge-site, the site hero wiring, and the CI job.

Not tested: didn't run the new Playwright suite (`bridge.spec.js`, `guest.spec.js`) or `scripts/prepare-assets.sh` in this session. The `deploy-bridge` job also can't be exercised until the Cloudflare Pages project is created.

output.title: Rewrite AGENTS.md as MUST rules, add Operations Graph incident memory
output.body:
AGENTS.md is rewritten into explicit MUST/MUST NOT sections so any agent (Codex, Claude Code, others) gets the same rules without depending on chat history, and a new `operations/` Operations Graph records past CI/production incidents as evidence-backed JSON instead of prose. This was driven directly by INC-2026-003: `MAX_TOPIC_REGENERATIONS = 6` was hardcoded in three independent regression assertions long after `ci_hotfix.py` moved production to `19`, and the same drift recurred across PR #430 and #426.

Behavior changes
- `ci_writer_observable_opening_hotfix.py:_hook_restates_question()`: markerless-hook overlap threshold tightened `0.80` → `0.50`, restoring the stricter boundary after "비행기 창문 모서리는 둥급니다" slipped through as a non-restatement at 0.80.
- Three stale `"MAX_TOPIC_REGENERATIONS = 6"` assertions updated to the current production value `19`: `quality/aviation_candidate_context_regression_test.py`, `quality/candidate_pool_handoff_regression_test.py`, `.github/workflows/candidate_pool_handoff_regression.yml`.

AGENTS.md
- Rewritten (275 lines) into Authority, Minimal Change, Engine Contracts, Quality, Budget, Regression, External Provider, Landing, and Production/Publishing Boundary sections.
- No longer hardcodes threshold numbers (hook floors, semantic_match, API/cost caps); points to their real source files instead, since ~48 `ci_*_hotfix.py` scripts rewrite these at CI runtime and `final_visual_director.py`'s `semantic_match` floor is domain-conditional.

Operations Graph (`operations/`)
- `schema.json` defines one incident record: run/job IDs, commit SHAs, PR numbers, a controlled root-cause category, and a limited relationship vocabulary (`RELATED_TO`, `SAME_SIGNATURE_AS`, `REGRESSION_OF`, `SUPERSEDES`).
- `query.py` is a deterministic, network-free CLI (`--failure-signature`, `--file`, `--root-cause`, `--related`, `--list`); `validate.py` enforces schema, evidence-completeness for `confidence`, and relationship integrity — `VERIFIED` requires real run/job id + signature, a real commit SHA, and a real `PASS`-ing post-fix workflow run, not just an assertion.
- 4 seed incidents in `incidents/*.json`: INC-2026-001 (Pexels 429 crash, `PARTIAL` — original failure run/job id not re-opened), INC-2026-002 (provider_state `TypeError` regression caught within PR #436, `VERIFIED`), INC-2026-003 (this `MAX_TOPIC_REGENERATIONS` drift, `VERIFIED`), INC-2026-004 (candidate rewrite-loop budget exhaustion from PR #426, `PARTIAL`).
- New `.github/workflows/operations_graph_validation.yml` runs `validate.py`, the regression suite, `py_compile`, and a `query.py --list` smoke test on every PR against `main`.

No engine, Candidate Explorer, rendering, provider, or budget/cost-cap behavior is touched beyond the two items above.

Tested:
- `python operations/validate.py` → PASS (4 incidents)
- `PYTHONPATH=. python quality/operations_graph_regression_test.py` → 13/13 passed
- `PYTHONPATH=. python -m quality.production_hotfix_chain_structure_regression_test` → PASS
- `python -m py_compile` on every new/changed Python file
- `yaml.safe_load` on the new workflow file
- `git fetch` + `rev-parse origin/main` immediately before commit: unchanged at `11c151fa80d4fc5ad7e0525cb4c458dafeadfe34`
